qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dominant North American pro-painter distribution moat backed by 5,000+ company-owned paint stores, proprietary tinting/formulations, jobsite delivery, and dedicated commercial trade credit. Paint represents only ~10-15% of total painting job costs while labor is 85-90%, making contractor switching economically irrational due to high failure risk and application downtime. Pricing power is empirically demonstrated by cumulative >25% price realization across 2021-2023 with gross margins expanding above 48% and 5-year median GAAP ROIC exceeding 22.8% (tangible ROIC >100%). Primary long-term erosion risks are prolonged deep freezes in housing turnover or aggressive commercial encroachment by big-box retailers.

qualitative.evidence: Sherwin-Williams generates 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 22.8% and tangible operating ROIC >100% on $23.6B in revenues. FCF conversion stands at 94.1% ($2.65B Owner FCF vs $2.57B Net Income in FY2025). The Paint Stores Group (PSG) operates 5,000+ company-owned locations, creating an insurmountable local delivery and trade credit moat that big-box retailers cannot replicate. Successfully proved pricing power by pushing cumulative price hikes >25% in 2021-2023, expanding gross margin from 42% to 48.5%. Balance sheet holds $9.32B long-term debt against $2.57B net income (3.63x) with EBIT interest coverage of 8.18x, maintaining a 47-year consecutive dividend growth streak and active share repurchases.
